summary: Albert Whitted Airport is a historic general aviation facility situated on the downtown waterfront of St. Petersburg, Florida, just steps from Tampa Bay. Named after pioneering aviator Albert Whitted, it has served the region since the early 20th century and remains one of the oldest operating airports in the Tampa Bay area. Today it primarily handles private aircraft, flight training, and recreational flying, offering spectacular waterfront views on approach.
faqs:
Q: Does Albert Whitted Airport offer commercial airline service?
A: No, Albert Whitted is a general aviation airport with no scheduled commercial flights. It serves private pilots, flight schools, and recreational aviation.

Q: How close is the airport to downtown St. Petersburg?
A: The airport sits right on the southeastern edge of downtown St. Petersburg, with the city center just minutes away by car or on foot.

Q: Are there any museums or attractions near the airport?
A: Yes, the St. Petersburg Museum of History is located adjacent to the airport, and the Dali Museum, pier, and waterfront parks are all within walking distance.

Q: Can visitors watch aircraft at Albert Whitted?
A: Absolutely. The airport has public viewing areas and a popular waterfront park where plane spotters can watch takeoffs and landings over Tampa Bay.
transport_tips: Driving is the most convenient way to reach Albert Whitted, with easy access from I-275 via exits for downtown St. Petersburg. Limited public transit options exist via the Pinellas Suncoast Transit Authority (PSTA) bus routes serving the downtown area. Rideshare services like Uber and Lyft are readily available and provide quick trips from Tampa International Airport, located about 20 miles northeast.
local_tip: Visit during sunset for one of the best plane-spotting experiences in Florida—small aircraft silhouetted against the sky over Tampa Bay make for stunning photographs, and you can grab dinner at nearby Beach Drive restaurants afterward.
